mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of periods with sustained GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening labor market, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within a month signals increased economic activity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and retail sales signals a strong consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer-driven sectors benefit.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between HOUST and RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls signals a strengthening labor market, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.5% and PAYEMS increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between UNRATE decreases, PAYEMS increases, and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index by more than 0.5% within a month signals inflationary pressure, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate coupled with an increase in real GDP signals a robust economic environment, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.5% and GDPC1 increases > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint correlation between UNRATE decreases, GDPC1 increases, and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
